text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Jordan celebrates 45th anniversary of King Hussein's accession to throne.
- Prime Minister Majali says government will not close door to dialogue with any political power.
- Finance Minister Hafez expects budget deficit of 3.1 percent and customs duties down to 30 percent next year.
- Interior Minister Rasheed says 146,000 new voters have registered for November parliamentary elections.
- Minister of State for Information Mutawae says inciting election boycott is illegal.
- Foreign Minister Tarawnah says progress in Middle East peace talks depends on security cooperation and lifting siege on Palestinian territories.
- Allenby Bridge between West Bank and Jordan is open to arrivals and departures.
- Israeli Jordan Valley settlers protest on Sheikh Hussein Bridge into Jordan against Israeli government's failure to provide subsidies for farms.
- Iraqi Trade Minister Saleh accuses United States of costing Jordan contracts under oil-for-food deal.
